notes.note: Starting with Firefox 156, Firefox Nightly enables Vulkan hardware video decoding on Linux for recent NVIDIA graphics cards.
Starting with Firefox 156, in Nightly builds, the search bar on the new tab is a real search bar now, showing results on the page instead of sending you to the address bar.

Starting with Firefox 159, [Firefox Nightly on Android][1] automatically turns on DNS over HTTPS for users in the United States, as Firefox on desktop does, unless network checks indicate it should stay off.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix
On macOS, sharing now uses the native macOS share picker, with AirDrop, Messages, and other apps available through an updated interface, and several selected tabs can be shared at once.

You can now search your open tabs with a keyboard shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+A on Windows and Linux, Cmd+Shift+A on macOS. The Extensions and Themes shortcut is now Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, and Cmd+Shift+E on macOS. You can change these shortcuts in about:keyboard.
Starting with Firefox 159, Firefox Nightly on macOS selects the word or link under the pointer when right-clicking like other macOS apps.
Web addresses written in the Javanese, Balinese, Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics and N'Ko scripts are now displayed in their own script instead of as encoded "xn--" text.
Starting with Firefox 156, in Nightly builds the centering of content inside buttons and text inputs is now expressed with `align-content` in the built-in stylesheet, so pages can override it.

Starting with Firefox 156, Firefox Nightly supports [Scoped Custom Element Registries][1]. Those registries can be created using the `CustomElementRegistry()` constructor that are separate from the global `window.customElements` registry. Creating more than one registry is useful for multiple custom elements that have the same tag name to coexist.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Web_components/Using_custom_elements#scoped_custom_element_registries

Starting with Firefox 158, Firefox Nightly supports the [`corner-shape`][1] property, including all `corner-*-shape` longhand properties, allowing to change the shape of the corners of an element.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/corner-shape

Starting with Firefox 158, Firefox Nightly now supports the [`random()`][1] CSS function, which allows authors to introduce randomness into their styles, generating a random value in a given range (with an optional increment) that is usable anywhere that math functions can be specified.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/random

Starting with Firefox 158, Firefox Nightly now supports streaming uploads with the [Fetch API][1], allowing web applications to send request bodies incrementally using a [`ReadableStream`][2] without buffering the entire body first.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API/Using_Fetch
  [2]: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/fetch-streaming-requests

Added support for Scoped Custom Element Registries. Those registries can be created using the `CustomElementRegistry()` constructor that are separate from the global `window.customElements` registry. Creating more than one registry is useful for multiple custom elements that have the same tag name to coexist.

Firefox now supports scroll-driven animations, so CSS animations can progress with the scroll position of a container or with an element's visibility as it scrolls into view, using the `animation-timeline`, `scroll-timeline`, `view-timeline`, and `animation-range` properties and the `ScrollTimeline` and `ViewTimeline` interfaces.

The [Sanitizer API][1] now sanitizes while parsing rather than the reified tree, extending sanitizing to scoped registries and declarative shadow roots.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/HTML_Sanitizer_API
WebGL 2 now supports the `EXT_texture_norm16` extension on compatible devices, adding 16-bit normalized texture and renderbuffer formats.
The Web Console now allows `let`, `const`, and `class` variables to be declared again, so a snippet can be edited and re-run without a redeclaration error.
Gamepad input on macOS is now delivered as soon as it happens, so quick button taps in web games register reliably.
Fixed tabs sometimes detaching into a new window when clicked on Linux with Wayland.
Fixed long drop-down lists on web pages sometimes showing blank space in place of the last options until the list was scrolled.
Fixed menus and panels fading in on Windows and Linux when animation effects are turned off in the operating system.
Fixed some videos displaying incorrectly on Windows when NVIDIA RTX Video HDR is enabled.
Importing from Google Chrome with a signed in Google account now detects and imports bookmarks.
Fixed pages on some sites, such as Slack, failing to load when the site rejected an HTTP/3 request, instead of retrying with HTTP/2.
Fixed the Replace button in Apple Writing Tools on macOS inserting the clipboard contents instead of the rewritten text on some sites, such as Gmail.
Fixed the file upload dialog opening in the last folder a file was saved to, such as Downloads, instead of the folder last used for uploads.

system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Nightly gets updated every day and as a consequence, the release notes for the Nightly channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports.
Warning: Features listed here may or may not make a final release of Firefox

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development on our [@FirefoxNightly][1] Bluesky account, our [@FirefoxNightly][4] Mastodon account as well as read our [Nightly Blog][2]. You can interact with other Firefox Nightly users and give your feedback to Mozilla staff in the [Nightly Matrix room][3] on chat.mozilla.org. [1]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxnightly.bsky.social [2]: https://blog.nightly.mozilla.org [3]: https://chat.mozilla.org/?#/room/#nightly:mozilla.org [4]: https://mastodon.social/@FirefoxNightly
